facts.text: Heritage Park opened in 2004, featuring a Tudor‑style Wickers Building from 1919, a 1917 superintendent cottage, and a restored Interurban trolley car.
Heritage Park also hosts free tours of the historic trolley and offers a comic book that tells Lynnwood’s early history.
Lynnwood High School originally sat next to Alderwood Mall before moving a mile east to North Road in northern Bothell in 2008.
The city’s borders run south to Mountlake Terrace, west to Edmonds, north to Picnic Point‑North Lynnwood, and east to Alderwood Manor along State Route 525.
Lynnwood falls within the Seattle–Tacoma media market, receiving news from The Seattle Times and local TV stations like KOMO‑TV and KING‑TV.
The first civic center buildings, including city hall and the public library, opened in 1971 and later expanded to house a police station and courthouse.
